registered_at: see the git commit that adds this file (06/11, +0700)
registered_before: any score of this token alphabet on the official recordings of LID-DS 2021 is computed; the alphabet runs so far read development recordings only
owner_decisions: 01/11: the goal is an ML model that detects blind attacks; rule paths set aside until the ML is decided
01/11: recall >= 95 %, precision >= 95 %, latency <= 3 s; benign-binary flagging and burden as low as possible
05/11: the official split may be scored a second time without a separate request; it is recorded here as such
seen_before_registration: lidds-ml-v2 official result (95.99 % recall, 0.57 % false alarms; the same official recordings, scored once on 05/11); on development with attack labels: the token alphabet study (9 alphabets), the inventory of syscall exits, the token variants on 6 weak scenarios (log2 size without halving best) and the full-resolution alphabets full1, select1, select1f (validation-evidence/results-20261105/ml-exploration/alphabets.txt, inventory.txt, variants.txt, select.txt, select1.txt). The errno set and the size resolution were chosen there, so the development numbers are optimistic. This is the second official scoring of an ML on LID-DS 2021; the official split is not unseen; the unseen evidence remains the live run and LID-DS 2019

model.token_alphabet: select1f (scripts/analysis/lidds_ml_token_alphabets.py): every syscall exit is a token; errno only for the listed syscalls; open mode and first directory for open, openat, openat2, creat; log2 of the returned byte count, not halved, for reads and writes; otherwise the name
model.why_this_alphabet: on development it equals the full alphabet at full size resolution (full1: 97.43 %, 19/3,403) while it needs exit information of these syscalls, the opens, the reads and the writes only, which a probe can hook per syscall instead of on every exit (a hook on every exit failed the overhead limit on 31/10)
model.language_model_and_score: as lidds-ml-v2: per-thread 4-grams, Witten-Bell backoff to P(name) x P(token | name), window score = mean of the 10 highest per-event negative log-probabilities
model.current_ml: as lidds-ml-v2: reference tree and support model of the 249 count features, warm-up gate lifted (lidds_ml_scores.py --all-windows)

decision: as lidds-ml-v2: per branch, moment-Gumbel quantile of the per-recording maximum over the validation recordings at alpha / 3; one window above it fires; no tripwire, novelty gate, vote or two-window rule
selection: the highest development recall among eligible; ties to fewer false alarms (lidds_ml_v2.py --token-column select1f)
verification_levels: as lidds-ml-v2: recall >= 95 % by the Wilson lower bound needs at least 1,223/1,271; false alarms <= 0.8 % by the upper bound needs at most about 50/7,938
reported_only: the same rule with the full1 alphabet (errno of every syscall), to show what the reduced hook set costs
limits: offline on sysdig traces; the probe does not collect these tokens yet and its overhead is unmeasured; futex is a hot syscall and its exit hook may cost most
the errno set and the size resolution were chosen on development with attack labels
code: scripts/analysis/lidds_ml_token_alphabets.py (tokens, ALL=1 run of scripts/lidds_ml_alphabets_run.sh), scripts/analysis/lidds_ml_v2.py --token-column select1f --protocol sentinel_pulse/protocol/lidds-ml-v3.json; --official refuses an existing output
